posts.text:
New flagstone patio by the pool in Hallsville, TX.

This family wanted a spot to sit around a fire at night now that summer is winding down, so our crew built a rounded flagstone patio off the end of their pool deck.

We started with chopped stone borders, set by hand to a string line and checked with a level so the edge stays true. Inside the border went a crushed limestone base, raked out solid and even. The flagstone they picked went on top, with every piece fit by hand and the joints filled.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New sprinkler system and Bermuda sod in Longview, TX.

This yard had more dirt than grass. Our crew trenched across it for the irrigation pipe, cutting through concrete with a saw where a line had to cross, then set the valves so each part of the yard waters on its own zone.

Track loaders brought in about 30 yards of topsoil and spread it evenly. About 32 sprinkler heads went in and the system was tested. Last came 19 pallets of Bermuda sod, laid by hand piece by piece. Installs are done under a Texas Licensed Irrigator.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New 90-foot flagstone walkway with path lights in Kilgore, TX.

This homeowner wanted one solid path tying the house to the back porch, ready to connect to whatever they build next. Our crew spread a crushed limestone base with a track loader and compacted it with a plate compactor.

Chopped stone borders were shaped, mortared and set by hand down both sides, then flagstone filled the space between them, fit piece by piece. Two new flower beds went in along the walkway with six azaleas. To finish, we ran electrical wire along both sides up to the back porch and set path lights along the way.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.
